1. Code 16: Defense (Core Focus)
Why it fits: Shipbuilding and fleet expansion fall directly under national security strategy, military force structure, and navy readiness.
Key Subtopics to Filter:
1610 — Procurement: Covers naval ship construction programs, defense industrial base capacity, defense contracts, and weapons systems acquisition.
1604 — Readiness: Covers fleet maintenance backlog, sealift capabilities, and deployment availability.
1617 — Contractors: Covers defense industry supply chains, shipyard contracting oversight, and government-contractor relationships.


2. Code 10: Transportation (Commercial Maritime & Industrial Base)
Why it fits: Non-military merchant marine capabilities, domestic shipyards, and commercial waterways fall under maritime policy. Navy readiness relies heavily on the commercial shipyard ecosystem (such as Jones Act regulations and dual-use industrial infrastructure).
Key Subtopic to Filter:
1007 — Maritime: Covers maritime shipping, inland waterways, commercial fleet maintenance, and domestic shipyard regulations.
1010 — Infrastructure: Covers port facilities, dockyard infrastructure, and public works supporting marine logistics.
